item.title: Her Sister Says A Sweater Sat Untested For Months
item.description: Ashley Loring HeavyRunner, 20, vanished from Montana’s Blackfeet Reservation in June 2017. Her sister told Congress that a sweater believed to be Ashley’s remained in evidence without being sent for testing. Her disappearance remains unsolved, with the FBI and BIA investigating.

item.title: She Crashed Her Car And Vanished Before Police Arrived
item.description: Nursing student Maura Murray, 21, disappeared after a crash in Haverhill, New Hampshire, on February 9, 2004. When police arrived, her car was there but she was gone. Despite extensive searches, her whereabouts remain unknown, and the FBI continues to seek tips.

item.title: The ‘Hiccup Girl’ Got Life Without Firing A Shot
item.description: Jennifer Mee became famous for her persistent hiccups before luring Shannon Griffin, 22, into a fatal robbery in Florida in 2010. Although she did not shoot him, she was convicted of first-degree murder and sentenced to life without parole in 2013.

item.title: She Faked Her Death And Returned As Her Own Twin
item.description: While wanted in Alabama, Marie Hilley faked her death and returned to her new husband as her imaginary twin. A false obituary helped expose her. In 1983, she received life for poisoning her first husband with arsenic and 20 years for attempting to murder her daughter.

item.title: A Tranquilizer Clue Led Back To Suzanne Morphew’s Husband
item.description: Suzanne Morphew vanished in Colorado in 2020. Animal tranquilizers found in her remains became key evidence when her husband, Barry, was charged again with murder in June 2025. Prosecutors allege he had access to the drugs. He has pleaded not guilty and awaits trial.

item.title: She Returned A Page, Then Left With An Unidentified Man
item.description: Georgia Leah Moses, 12, disappeared from Santa Rosa in August 1997. Her body was found nine days later near a highway. Her sister, Angel Turner, continues seeking answers in the unsolved murder, for which California renewed a $50,000 reward in 2026.

item.title: A Juror’s Family Tie Overturned Her Murder Conviction
item.description: Letecia Stauch was convicted in 2023 of killing her 11-year-old stepson, Gannon, in Colorado. In April 2026, an appeals court overturned her conviction because a juror’s son-in-law worked for the prosecuting office. The state has sought Supreme Court review of that ruling.

item.title: She Spoke With Police For 45 Minutes, Then Disappeared
item.description: Emma Fillipoff, 26, disappeared from Victoria, British Columbia, on November 28, 2012, after police spoke with her outside the Empress Hotel and determined she was safe to leave. Her van was later found with most of her belongings inside. She remains missing.
